knowledgeAnswers.rationale: Flagging keeps the visit visible so a person can resolve it with the customer.
Grouping pulls nearby visits together so workers spend less time travelling.
Both tools can move agreed bookings, so a person needs to confirm the customer's window still holds.

practicalCriteria: Learner completes the core task of this lesson in the training environment (clash handling, grouping nearby visits and gap filling) and the assessor confirms each record matches the procedure.
Learner explains, in their own words, what each record is for and which record they would change in a given situation.
Learner shows one correction they made to a sample record and says why it was needed.
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Knowledge check result recorded for the learner
Assessor observation of the practical criteria in the training environment
Sample record (screenshot or printed copy) kept by the assessor
stopWorkCriteria: Stop before dispatch or booking if a visit window, worker or site detail cannot be confirmed.
Stop and tell the owner if a record shows a customer or site hazard that is not yet in the job record.
